sources: CFFfertility women:retained fertility,increased pregnancies in modulator era,contraception

choiceReview.text: Fertility, contraception, pregnancy, lactation, genetic counseling, and mental health belong in routine CF care rather than crisis-only conversations.
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Discuss fertility only after an unplanned pregnancy and mood only after hospitalization.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Assume CF prevents pregnancy and therefore removes the need for contraceptive counseling.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Treat a modulator response as a reason to stop reproductive and mental health review.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: Routine anticipatory review supports informed decisions and coordinated care. Waiting for pregnancy or hospitalization loses preparation time; CF does not ensure infertility; improved lung function does not remove reproductive or mental health needs.

sources: CFFfertility women:retained fertility,increased pregnancies in modulator era,contraception

choiceReview.text: Discuss reproductive goals and emotional health proactively, then coordinate medications and support with the CF and specialty teams.
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Wait for a positive pregnancy test before reconciling medication exposure.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Screen for depression only when the patient volunteers a crisis.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Stop every CF medication automatically when pregnancy is being considered.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: Proactive discussion connects personal goals, medication assessment, and support. Preconception review should precede a positive test; annual screening begins at age 12 rather than depending on a crisis; pregnancy requires an individual product and clinical benefit-risk plan, not automatic discontinuation of every therapy.

sources: CFFfertility women:retained fertility,increased pregnancies in modulator era,contraception

choiceReview.text: Review fertility, contraception, pregnancy, lactation, genetics, medication exposure, interactions, mood, anxiety, sleep, support, and patient goals.
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Review fertility alone and omit medication exposure and mental health.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Review mood alone and assume contraception is unnecessary in CF.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Review prescriptions alone and omit pregnancy, lactation, support, and patient goals.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: The complete assessment addresses reproduction, exposures, emotional health, implementation, and preferences. Fertility-only review misses interactions and mental health; mood-only review omits pregnancy prevention; a prescription list alone cannot establish reproductive risks or practical support.

sources: CFFfertility women:retained fertility,increased pregnancies in modulator era,contraception

choiceReview.text: Waiting for pregnancy or a mental health crisis can remove time to optimize therapy, counseling, and support.
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Discussing contraception before a pregnancy occurs.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Obtaining annual PHQ-9 and GAD-7 screening from age 12.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Arranging CF and obstetric medication review before conception.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: The hazard is postponing planning until pregnancy or crisis. Contraception discussion, age-appropriate annual screening, and preconception medication review are safeguards that preserve time for informed choices and support.

choiceReview.text: Advanced-lung-disease support and transplant referral should begin from trajectory and complications while the patient still has physiologic reserve.
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Refer only after terminal failure because earlier evaluation commits the person to surgery.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Use the adult FEV1 threshold unchanged for every child.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Assume improved modulator response permanently removes all transplant indications.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: Trajectory and complications support timely advanced care and referral. Referral does not commit the patient to surgery; under-18 thresholds differ from adult thresholds; modulator response requires reassessment but cannot guarantee that transplantation will never be indicated.

choiceReview.text: Coordinate oxygen, ventilation, pulmonary rehabilitation, complication planning, goals of care, and timely transplant evaluation.
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Start oxygen and BiPAP for every patient solely because FEV1 is low.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Defer rehabilitation and goals-of-care discussion until listing is complete.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Treat palliative care as a requirement to stop CF treatment and transplant evaluation.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: Coordinate support according to documented physiology, complications, and patient goals. Oxygen addresses hypoxemia and nocturnal NIV may address chronic hypercarbia, with restrictions such as active pneumothorax; rehabilitation and planning need not wait for listing; palliative care can accompany usual treatment and transplant planning.

choiceReview.text: Review FEV1 trajectory, exacerbations, oxygen, hypercapnia, ventilation, nutrition, function, hemoptysis, pneumothorax, pulmonary hypertension, contraindications, and goals.
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Review one current FEV1 value and omit trajectory and complications.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Review oxygen saturation alone and omit carbon dioxide, function, and nutritional status.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Review transplant barriers alone and assume any unresolved barrier prohibits referral.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: Multidomain review identifies severity and supports shared referral decisions. One FEV1 value misses decline and complications; oxygen alone misses hypercarbia and reserve; barriers need optimization but unresolved barriers do not automatically prohibit referral.

choiceReview.text: Waiting for terminal respiratory failure before transplant referral can leave inadequate time for evaluation, optimization, and listing.
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Beginning transplant discussion when FEV1 falls below 50% predicted.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Evaluating survival markers even when FEV1 has not reached 30% predicted.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Addressing modifiable barriers while referring to a transplant center.
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: Waiting for terminal failure can lose time for evaluation and optimization. Discussion below 50%, assessment of survival markers beyond FEV1, and concurrent barrier reduction are appropriate safeguards; referral is distinct from listing and surgery.

sources: CFF2013 IPC official recommendations:hand hygiene,contact regardless cultures,six feet household exception,masks,waiting areas,psychosocial impact

choiceReview.text: Maintain at least six feet of separation and use the clinic mask and contact-precaution plan
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Permit close contact because both cultures are negative
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Separate them only if both have the same cultured organism
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Apply the same-household exception because they attend the same clinic
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: The separation rule applies regardless of culture results. Negative cultures do not remove precautions, matching organisms is not a condition for separation, and sharing a clinic does not make two people members of the same household.

choiceReview.text: Annual PHQ-9 and GAD-7 screening with a pathway for clinical assessment and treatment
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Wait until age 18 to screen
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Screen only if a pulmonary exacerbation requires admission
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Diagnose depression automatically from any nonzero screening score
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: Annual screening begins at age 12 even without a volunteered concern. Waiting until 18 or hospitalization misses that recommendation. Screening findings require clinical assessment; a nonzero score is not itself a depression diagnosis.

sources: CFFreviewJuly2025:no update needed;consensus and absent-consensus distinctions retained

choiceReview.text: Stop airway clearance and inhaled hypertonic saline, and withhold BiPAP
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Continue all airway clearance because bleeding always improves with secretion movement
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Stop hypertonic saline only and continue BiPAP unchanged
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Manage as scant hemoptysis because the threshold for massive bleeding is 500 mL
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: 300 mL exceeds the greater-than-240-mL massive threshold and requires admission. The guideline stops airway clearance and hypertonic saline and withholds BiPAP. Continuing clearance or BiPAP misses these restrictions, and 500 mL is not the stated threshold. Stabilization and specialist decisions remain urgent.

sources: CFFreviewJuly2025:no update needed;consensus and absent-consensus distinctions retained

choiceReview.text: Withhold BiPAP while the pneumothorax persists and avoid positive expiratory pressure; aerosols need not stop solely because of pneumothorax
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Continue BiPAP but stop all nebulized medicines automatically
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Continue positive expiratory pressure because only hemoptysis changes airway therapy
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Treat every airway method and aerosol as subject to the same mandatory stopping rule
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: Active pneumothorax requires withholding BiPAP and avoiding positive expiratory pressure or intrapulmonary percussive ventilation. The guideline does not require stopping aerosols solely for pneumothorax and lacks consensus on every other clearance method. The alternatives invert those restrictions, ignore pressure-related restrictions, or invent a universal stopping rule.

choiceReview.text: Refer for lung transplant evaluation while continuing optimization and shared planning
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Wait until FEV1 is below 30% because exacerbations do not affect referral
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Wait for terminal respiratory failure to prove eligibility
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Refer only if every modifiable barrier has already resolved
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: FEV1 below 40% with more than two IV-treated exacerbations per year meets a referral recommendation. Waiting for below 30% ignores this trigger, terminal failure risks losing evaluation time, and unresolved modifiable barriers do not automatically prevent referral. Evaluation does not itself mean listing or immediate transplantation.

choiceReview.text: Refer no later than FEV1 below 40% predicted for a person under 18
choiceReview.finding: Supported best answer in the specified context

choiceReview.text: Apply the adult below-30% threshold and defer referral
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Require an additional survival marker before any referral below 40% in a child
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

choiceReview.text: Defer discussion because FEV1 is still above 30%
choiceReview.finding: Incorrect premise or inappropriate action individually explained in rationale

wholeQuestionReview.individualAlternativeReasoning: For patients under 18, referral is recommended no later than FEV1 below 40% even without an additional marker. The adult below-30% threshold is not the pediatric rule, an extra survival marker is not required at this threshold, and transplant discussion should already occur below 50%.

question.question: Why should lung transplant referral occur before terminal respiratory failure?
choices: Evaluation, optimization, and listing require time while the patient still has reserve
CFTR modulators eliminate every transplant indication
A single low spirometry value is the only criterion
question.rationale: Early referral allows evaluation, barrier reduction, and shared decisions while physiologic reserve remains. Referral does not mean immediate surgery or listing, modulator benefit does not eliminate every indication, and age, trajectory, complications, and survival markers matter beyond a single spirometry value.
